issues: The definition frames the word as pushing two parties toward reconciliation, but the syntactic role data shows the single occurrence is vocative, not a transitive drive/push construction — the definition implies active transitive force that may not match actual usage
The sense label '1. urging two people together' does not match the measured sense label '1. two' — the corpus label appears to be a fragment or error rather than a meaningful gloss

The definition does not acknowledge that the critical text (SBLGNT) reads συνήλλασσεν instead, making this lemma's NT presence textually disputed at 0 occurrences in the primary critical edition — this is mentioned in the article but not the definition itself
The definition omits the directional phrase εἰς εἰρήνην ('toward peace') that is integral to understanding how the word functions in its only attested NT context

receipts.how: The sole Byzantine-text occurrence, where Moses attempts to reconcile two quarreling Israelites εἰς εἰρήνην, demonstrates the figurative reconciliation sense the definition captures, but also shows the textual dispute since SBLGNT reads συνήλλασσεν here instead
Abbott-Smith notes this is a Received Text reading replaced by WH and RV with συνήλλασσεν, confirming the definition's core claim holds only conditionally on text-critical grounds

The SBLGNT reading συνήλλασσεν (conative imperfect, 'was trying to reconcile') actually better explains the reconciliation nuance than συνελαύνω's 'drive together' frame, showing the definition slightly overstates the coercive-force aspect
